title: Finite point fibres of an affine chart and its relation over a relatively quasi-separated space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with field-valued point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose the representable relative diagonal $X\to X\times_SX$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests, meaning that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Let $a:W\to X$ be representable etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], where $W$ is an affine scheme (isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), and assume the composite $W\to S$ factors through an affine open of $S$. Put $R=W\times_XW$ with projections $s,t:R\to W$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every $x\in|X|$, both sets $\{w\in W:a(w)=x\}$ and $\{r\in R:a(s(r))=x\}$ are finite. Empty fibres are allowed; neither $a$ nor $W\to S$ is assumed surjective, and no finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03JX, lemma-bounded-fibres: (zeta) implies (gamma); Tag 03JV, lemma-UR-finite-above-x, condition (1). The relative-diagonal hypothesis gives Zariski local absolute quasi-separatedness by spaces-properties.tex Tag 03W7, lemma-quasi-separated-quasi-compact-pieces, (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Fix $x\in|X|$. If $x$ is outside the image of $|W|\to|X|$, the first fibre is empty and so is the second, since $R\to X$ factors through $W$. Otherwise choose $w\in W$ above $x$. The point convention [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] gives its residue-field representative $T=\operatorname{Spec}F\to W$, where $F=\kappa(w)$, and hence $j:T\to X$ representing $x$. The spectrum $T$ has one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V\subset S$ be the affine open through which $W\to S$ factors. The chosen map $T\to W\to S$ also factors through $V$. No quasi-compactness or monomorphism property of $j$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03JV, lemma-UR-finite-above-x, the field representative in the proof of (5) implies (1); choose it through a chart point.

proof.text: Put $B=W\times_ST$. Since both maps factor through the open subscheme $V$, this is $W\times_VT$: maps into the restricted locally ringed space $V$ are determined by their composites to $S$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Both factors and $V$ are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] makes $B$ affine, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Put $P=W\times_XT$. Its map to $B$ is the scheme test of $\Delta_{X/S}$ along the map $B\to X\times_SX$ induced by $(a,j)$. Indeed, on each test scheme both pullbacks consist of pairs $(u,v)$ with $a(u)=j(v)$, using the sheaf fibre product [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The relative-diagonal hypothesis therefore makes $P\to B$ quasi-compact. The inverse image of the whole quasi-compact open $B$ is $P$, so $P$ is quasi-compact. By the scheme-test definition [def-trf-algebraic-space], $P$ is a scheme and $p:P\to T$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 03W7, lemma-quasi-separated-quasi-compact-pieces, (1) implies (3), affine-product diagonal test; combined with decent-spaces.tex Tag 03JV field-pullback argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to $p:P\to T$ at the unique point of the field spectrum $T$. Its scheme fibre is $P$ itself, by the identity-base-change universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $|P|$ is discrete. The covering by its open singletons has a finite subcover because $P$ is quasi-compact, so $|P|$ is finite. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], the image of $|P|\to|W|$ is precisely $\{w\in W:a(w)=x\}$, since the image of $|T|\to|X|$ is $\{x\}$. This proves the first finiteness assertion, including an empty fibre.

source.place: Tag 03JV, lemma-UR-finite-above-x, (5) implies (1); morphisms.tex Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian.

proof.text: Put $Q=P\times_TP$ with projection $q:Q\to P$. The target $T$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $P$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $p$ quasi-compact; (3) makes its base change $q$ quasi-compact; (2) makes $Q$ quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1), $q$ is etale, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2) makes $p\circ q:Q\to T$ etale. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] at the unique point of $T$: again the fibre is the scheme itself, and $|Q|$ is discrete. Its singleton covering has a finite subcover, so $|Q|$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 03JV, lemma-UR-finite-above-x, (5) implies (1), paragraph on the quasi-compact etale field product; morphisms.tex Tags 02GO, 02GN, 02GL.

proof.text: The canonical identification $Q\cong R\times_XT$ is elementary from the sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. On any test scheme a section of $Q$ is a triple $(w_1,w_2,t)$ satisfying $a(w_1)=j(t)=a(w_2)$; the same triple is exactly a section of $(W\times_XW)\times_XT$. The two maps keep all three entries, so are natural inverse maps and commute with the projections to $R$. (Here $R\to X$ is $a\circ s=a\circ t$.) Apply [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] to $R\to X$ and $T\to X$: the image of $|R\times_XT|\to|R|$ is exactly $\{r\in R:a(s(r))=x\}$. This is the image of the finite set $|Q|$, so the second fibre is finite as well. If $P$ is empty, so is $Q$, and both asserted images are empty.

source.place: Tag 03JV, lemma-UR-finite-above-x, final argument of (5) implies (1), simplified using the monomorphism supplied by (4); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian.

tool_uses.why: The basic scheme fact supplies quasi-compactness of W and quasi-separatedness of Spec F; the unit does not reprove affine scheme topology.
Scheme quasi-compactness over a quasi-separated target and its base-change and source consequences make P times_F P quasi-compact.
Scheme etale base change supplies Q -> P; the unit uses the standard scheme etale calculus.
Scheme etale composition supplies Q -> Spec F.
The etale-over-a-field decomposition supplies discreteness of P and Q; no algebraic-space chart-fibre finiteness is taken from this node.
The general point-image formula for sheaf fibre products identifies the two desired set-theoretic fibres, rather than asserting that point functors preserve fibre products bijectively.
The general sheaf fibre-product construction provides R and the sectionwise identification Q = R times_X Spec F.
The elementary scheme affine-product theorem makes W times_S Spec F affine after restricting to the given affine base open V; it supplies no algebraic-space finiteness assertion.

Step 2: B=W x_S T=W x_V T because an open immersion is a monomorphism. B is affine by the affine-product lemma and so quasi-compact. P=W x_X T is the diagonal test over B (checked on sections), hence quasi-compact, and etale over Spec F. Step 3: by the etale-over-field lemma, |P| is discrete and quasi-compact, hence finite. The image formula of lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus gives the W-fibre; it identifies scheme points with point classes by the DAG convention, and the direction needed is elementary. Step 4: qcqs permanence clauses (1), (3) and (2) and etale base change/composition make Q=P x_T P finite. Step 5: Q = R x_X T via triples, and the image formula gives the R-fibre. lean.statement: theorem relative_qs_affine_chart_point_fibres {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hdiag : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ QuasiCompact p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 X.obj.obj) (𝟙 X.obj.obj))) (W : Over S) [IsAffine W.left] (a : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj) (ha : IsEtale a) (hbase : ∃ V : S.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ ∃ b : W.left ⟶ V.toScheme, b ≫ V.ι = W.hom) (R : Over S) (s t : R ⟶ W) (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) a a) : ∀ x : Point X.obj.obj, Set.Finite {w : W.left | schemePointMap a w = x} ∧ Set.Finite {r : R.left | schemePointMap (yoneda.map s ≫ a) r = x}
lean.note: The relation scheme and its projections are specified by a representing Yoneda pullback square; the conclusion holds for every such representation. The presheaf product on Over S is the relative product over S, so hdiag is exactly the representable relative-diagonal condition with scheme QuasiCompact tests.
